setup.title: Create your project
setup.description: Choose a name and the local folder your agents will work in.
setup.name: Project name
setup.folderHelp: Choose the folder of an existing git repository. Nothing is cloned or uploaded.
setup.folderHelpChosen: Agents work in this folder. Nothing is cloned or uploaded.
setup.detectedFromFolder: GitHub is detected from the folder
setup.detectedFromFolderDetail: Orchester reads the folder’s git remote (origin) and asks the GitHub CLI (gh) which account is signed in. GitHub is optional: without it, pull request steps are unavailable.

ownership.title: A home for this project’s work
ownership.detail: Tasks, agent profiles, instructions, tools, secrets and connections stay in this project. You can import independent copies from another project later.
ownership.detailNamed: Tasks, agent profiles, instructions, tools, secrets and connections stay in {{name}}. You can import independent copies from another project later.

bar.chooseFolder: Choose the project folder to continue.
bar.needsRepository: The project folder must be a git repository to continue.
bar.explanation: Creates the project in the repository’s .orchester folder and opens it.
bar.needsCommit: The project folder needs a first commit to continue.
bar.needsGit: Install git to continue: runs work in git worktrees.

github.title: GitHub repository
github.addConnectionUnavailable: Add the GitHub connection once the project exists, in its Connections.
github.runThis: Run this in a terminal, then check again.

heading.notSignedIn: gh is not signed in to {{host}}
heading.notRepository: This folder is not a git repository
heading.gitFailed: Couldn’t read the folder’s git remotes
heading.emptyRepository: The repository has no default branch yet

note.detected: {{project}} will expect {{account}}. Orchester uses gh’s own sign-in and never stores or sees a token.
note.detectedUnnamed: This project will expect {{account}}. Orchester uses gh’s own sign-in and never stores or sees a token.
note.detecting: Reading the folder’s git remote and asking gh about the repository. You can already create the project.
note.noRemote: You can create the project. Pull request steps and the Pull requests screen stay unavailable until the folder has a GitHub remote.
note.notGitHub: Pull request steps will be unavailable. If this is a GitHub Enterprise host, add a GitHub connection for it, then check again.
note.ghNotFound: Orchester reaches GitHub only through gh. Install it or choose its program file, then check again. You can create the project now.
note.notSignedIn: Run this in a terminal, then check again. Orchester never signs in for you.
note.wrongAccount: Switch gh back to {{expected}} in a terminal and check again, or make {{project}} expect {{active}}. Orchester never switches gh accounts; pull requests can’t be created until they match.
note.wrongAccountUnnamed: Switch gh back to {{expected}} in a terminal and check again, or make this project expect {{active}}. Orchester never switches gh accounts; pull requests can’t be created until they match.
note.noAccess: GitHub found no repository this account can read. Ask the owner for access, or switch accounts in gh, then check again.
note.unrecognized: gh answered in a format Orchester doesn’t recognise. Update gh, then check again. Details are in the log.
note.unrecognizedVersion: gh {{version}} answered in a format Orchester doesn’t recognise. Update gh, then check again. Details are in the log.
note.notRepository: Runs work in git worktrees, so the project folder must be a git repository. Initialise it in a terminal, or choose another folder, then check again. Create project & continue stays disabled until then.
note.missingScope: gh is signed in as {{account}} without the {{scope}} scope that Orchester needs to read and create pull requests. Add it in a terminal, then check again. You can create the project now.
note.gitFailed: git couldn’t read the folder’s remotes. Make sure git is installed, then check again.
note.couldNotRun: gh could not be started or did not answer in time. Check again.
note.unreachable: gh couldn’t reach {{host}}. Check the network, then check again.
note.rateLimited: GitHub’s API rate limit is used up. Check again later.
note.emptyRepository: Push a first commit to the repository, then check again.

access.title: Change GitHub account or access
access.detail: Orchester uses the account gh is signed in to on this computer. It never signs in, switches accounts or sees your token.
access.otherDetail: Sign in once, then switch. gh accounts are shared by every project on this computer.
access.accessDetail: Orchester needs the {{scope}} scope. If gh doesn’t have it, add it.
access.runHint: Run these in a terminal, then check again.

heading.notFound: git is not installed on this computer
heading.noCommits: This repository has no commits yet

note.notRepository: Runs work in git worktrees, so the project folder must be a git repository. Orchester can create one here, or you can choose another folder.
note.notFound: Orchester runs git to read the folder and to create a repository, and runs work in git worktrees. Install git, then check again.
note.commitFailed: Runs branch from a commit, so the project folder needs one. The repository is kept: Try again makes only the first commit.
note.noCommits: Runs branch from a commit, so the project folder needs one. Orchester can make the first commit here.

value.filesIgnored: {{count}} files · a .gitignore is in the folder
value.fileIgnored: 1 file · a .gitignore is in the folder

create.title: Create a git repository here
create.branchConfigured: git init on the branch {{branch}}, the name your git setting init.defaultBranch gives.
create.branchDefault: git init on the branch {{branch}}, since init.defaultBranch is not set.
create.branchChecking: git init on the branch your git setting init.defaultBranch names, or main.
create.then: Then a first commit, “Initial commit”, by the author git is set up with. Runs branch from a commit, and a new repository has none.
create.files: Commit the folder’s files as the first commit
create.filesDetailIgnored: Adds {{count}} files. The .gitignore in the folder is honoured: what it lists stays out of git.
create.fileDetailIgnored: Adds 1 file. The .gitignore in the folder is honoured: what it lists stays out of git.
create.filesEmpty: The folder is empty: there are no files to commit.
create.empty: Start with an empty first commit
create.emptyDetail: Nothing of the folder is committed yet. Runs start from this empty commit, so agents see none of the folder’s {{count}} files until you commit them.
create.emptyDetailOne: Nothing of the folder is committed yet. Runs start from this empty commit, so agents don’t see the folder’s file until you commit it.
create.emptyDetailUnknown: Nothing of the folder is committed yet. Runs start from this empty commit, so agents see none of the folder’s files until you commit them.
create.emptyDetailEmptyFolder: The repository starts with one commit that holds no files, for runs to branch from.
create.review: Review the files git will add; a .gitignore keeps files out.
create.unavailable: Create a git repository here needs git on this computer.
create.fallback: Or in a terminal: run git init and make a first commit, then check again.
create.fallbackCommit: Or in a terminal: make a first commit, then check again.
create.emptyStaged: Files are staged in this repository already, and an empty first commit would leave them out. Commit the folder’s files, or unstage them in a terminal.
create.inside: This folder is inside the git repository {{repository}}. Create a separate repository here, or choose {{repository}}.

progress.committingFiles: Committing {{count}} files as the first commit…
progress.committingFile: Committing 1 file as the first commit…
progress.committingUnknown: Committing the folder’s files as the first commit…

done.files: Created here with a first commit of {{count}} files.
done.file: Created here with a first commit of 1 file.
done.empty: Created here with an empty first commit.
done.unknown: Created here with a first commit.

error.gitMissing: git could not be started: it is no longer found on this computer. Install git, then check again.
error.notWritable: Couldn’t create the repository: {{folder}} can’t be written (permission denied). Choose a folder you can write to, or change its permissions, then try again.
error.alreadyRepository: The folder is a git repository already. Check again.
error.notRepository: The folder is no longer a git repository. Check again.
error.hasCommits: The repository has a commit already. Check again.
error.initStopped: git init did not finish. Try again.
error.addStopped: git add did not finish. Try again.
error.commitStopped: git commit did not finish. Try again.
error.staged: Files are staged in this repository, and an empty first commit would leave them out. Commit the folder’s files instead, or unstage them in a terminal, then try again.

identity.intro: Tell git who you are in a terminal, then try again. Orchester never changes git’s settings.
identity.name: git config --global user.name "Your Name"

install.intro: Install git in a terminal, then check again:
install.unsupported: Install git with this system’s package manager, then check again.
